**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE Date Issued: 21</mark>**<sup>**st**</sup> **<mark>June 2011</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for March 2011** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for March 2011 world copper supply and demand in its June 2011 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for March 2011 showed a small production surplus of 18,000 metric tonnes (t). When making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, March showed a larger surplus of 33,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first quarter 2011, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 33,000 t (a seasonally adjusted deficit of 16,000 t). This compares with a production surplus of 10,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of about 42,000 t) in the same quarter of 2010. 

During the first quarter of 2011, world apparent usage grew by 2.4% compared with that in the first quarter of 2010: A growth of 90% in Russia and a growth of around 4% each in the European Union, Japan and the United States were partially offset by a decline of 6% in China’s apparent usage*. China’s apparent usage decline in the 1<sup>st</sup> quarter 2011 reflects a 31% decrease in refined copper net imports from those in the first quarter of 2010, and the increase in Russia’s apparent usage reflected a 65% decline in net refined exports. On a regional basis, usage grew by 2.1% in Africa, 4.6% in the Americas, 10.9% in Europe, and 35% in Oceania and declined by 1.6% in Asia. 

World mine production grew by around 2.5% (93,000 t) in the first quarter of 2011 compared with that in the same quarter of 2010: Concentrate production grew by 3.8% while solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) declined by 2.4%. In part, this relative increase reflects operational constraints that reduced production in 2010 in Australia and Mexico. Production in Chile, the world’s leading producer, was down by 0.7%.  Production was also down in other major producers such as the United States (-3.5%), Indonesia (-18%) and the Democratic Republic of Congo (-16%). On a regional basis, mine production increased by 1.2% in the Americas, 7% in Europe, and 24% in Oceania but decreased by 1% in both Africa and Asia.  The mine capacity utilization rate increased slightly in March and the average for the 1<sup>st</sup> quarter of 2011 was practically unchanged from that in the same quarter of 2010. 

During the first quarter of 2011, world refined production grew by 1.5% as compared with that in the same quarter of 2010: Primary production increased by 1.2% and secondary production (from scrap) increased by 2.7%. Production increases of 71% in Australia (recovery from low 2010 level), 11% in China, and 6% in India were partially offset by declines in Chile (-3.5%), the United Sates (-12%), Canada (-27%) and Japan (-12%). Refined production capacity

utilization in the first quarter of 2011 was around 78% as compared with 79% in the same quarter of 2010. The average LME cash price for May 2011 was US$8,927.05 per tonne, down from the April 2011 average of US$9,483.25 per tonne. The 2011 high and low copper prices through the end of May were US$10,148 and US$8,536.5 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$9,147.26 per tonne. As of the end of May, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 626,651 t, an increase of 58,469 t from stocks held at the end of December 2010. Compared to the March levels, stocks were up at LME and down at Comex and SHFE.
